question: Which statement best describes Server state vs UI state?
options: Separate the data you fetch from the server (users, metrics) from ephemeral UI state (which row is selected, is the drawer open). Server state has loading/error/refetch lifecycles and is best owned by a data layer or cache (React Query/SWR), while UI state is local and disposable. Mixing them — e.g. copying fetched data into useState — leads to staleness and sync bugs.

Build the reusable pieces (Table, Modal, Tabs) as compound components that share state implicitly through Context, so consumers compose
without prop-drilling. This gives a flexible, readable API for the dashboard's many composite widgets. It pairs well with controlled/uncontrolled patterns for things like the selectable table.

Use a persistent layout shell (sidebar + topbar) with nested routes rendering into an <Outlet>, so navigation swaps only the page area while the shell stays mounted. This keeps scroll position and sidebar state intact and makes the URL the single source of truth for what's shown. Deep-linking to a filtered view or a specific user becomes trivial.

The filtered/sorted/paginated rows shown in the table should be computed from the source data plus the current search/filter/sort/page during render — not stored as their own state. Storing a derived copy creates a second source of truth that drifts when the data or filters change. Wrap expensive derivations in useMemo keyed on the inputs.
